title: Birth-site depletion makes distance per cycle pay for the Marangoni rods (40-55% of dividing rods swim 3 own lengths vs 10-25% in the sink-disc world and under the same supply loss spread everywhere, 3 of 3 seeds), but plastically: the identical-event twin passes almost as often, the heritable Marangoni trait does not rise and the gradient on distance per cycle is negative
summary: c50's spread world (self-copied mar 20/40/60 ladder, mar-40 founders, trait-blind mutation, sink discs) plus a depletion disc (R 20 px, target -0.7, 200 t) opened at every split site, read from the field and blind to kind, speed and displacement. On fresh seeds 600-602 the share of dividing rods passing the M gate is 7/15, 6/11, 6/15 against 1/11, 3/12, 1/16 when the same supply loss is spread over the domain and 4/17, 1/10, 3/20 in the sink-disc world; the drive-off arm with depletion makes 0 of 9 passers. But the identical-event twin (MARS 40/40/40) passes 3/11, 2/7, 7/16, the trait mean late is below the sink-disc world on 3 of 3 seeds and the descendants' gradient on distance per cycle is negative on 3 of 3: the environment raises the capability as a response of the ancestral kind, not by selecting the heritable trait. Negative for the challenge; the depletion rule is a candidate selective environment once the trait has variance (competition assay next).

finding.operator: depletion disc opened at each split site (trait-, speed- and displacement-blind) on the self-copied Marangoni ladder
finding.control: identical-event twin (MARS 40/40/40), global supply loss of equal size (DEP=2), sink-disc world without depletion, drive-off with depletion; paired seeds 600-602
